description_full: Amdocs Limited, through its subsidiaries, provides software and services to communications, entertainment, media, and other service providers worldwide. It designs, develops, operates, implements, supports, and markets open and modular cloud offering. The company also provides CES25, a telco-native, GenAI-led customer experience suite, spanning business, and operations and network domains that is embedded with AI and related tools. In addition, it offers GenAI agents, and which include Customer Engagement Platform, a telecom-specific customer relationship management (CRM) solution; Amdocs Monetization Suite which enables customers to monetize their broad set of services and offerings; Amdocs Intelligent Networking Suite, a set of solutions that provide end-to-end service orchestration; Amdocs Charging; Amdocs eSIM Cloud that enables service providers to offer digital SIM (eSIM); Amdocs MarketONE, a based Software-as-a-Service (SaaS)-based platform that includes pre-integrated digital services, ranging from media, gaming, eLearning, sports and retail to security, and business services; and Amdocs connectX, a cloud-native telco-in-a-box software-as-a-service platform for digital telecom brands, as well as Amdocs CatalogONE that spans the entire CES25 suite and combines embedded business intelligence with telecom-specific GenAI agents. Further, the company provides consulting, experience design, data, cloud, network services, delivery, quality engineering, operations, systems integration, and content services to various platforms and technologies; maintenance, enhancement design and development, and operational support services; network deployment and optimization services; and managed services, including AI and related tools, predictive analytics, and robotic process automation, as well as quality engineering, mobile network, cloud, and professional services. Amdocs Limited was founded in 1982 and is headquartered in Saint Louis, Missouri.

financial_summary: Amdocs Limited is a mid-cap technology business with a $4.7B market cap on $5.0B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +5% over the past three years and +4% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 16% against a 8% cost of capital, a 8-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it.

The business throws off $619M in free cash flow — roughly 12 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.47× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.2× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 18× is fortress-like.

Management returns a meaningful 16.6% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

sector_headwinds.text: Low reinvestment-driven growth suggests the compounding engine has stalled
Fragmented industry with below-average profit capture — no moat to protect margins
Above-average short interest at 9.7% of float
Insiders are net sellers (75% sell ratio) over the past year
Significant goodwill (45% of assets) from past acquisitions — a soft asset a conservative appraisal discounts to zero
Technology sector lagging the market significantly, underperforming by 7% over 3 months
Elevated sector volatility (38% annualized) adds uncertainty
Antitrust and platform-regulation risk — the larger the network effect, the larger the regulatory target on its back, and a single consent decree can reset the moat.
AI disruption of existing software moats — incumbents with durable margins face commoditisation as AI-native competitors replicate features at a fraction of the R&D cost.
Cybersecurity liability and talent cost inflation — a single breach can erase years of goodwill, and the war for engineering talent compresses margins even at scale.

sect: Its 13% operating margin runs 6pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It earns less of the sector's profit than its revenue share would suggest (0.54x).
It accounts for 0.1% of sector revenue and 0.1% of sector operating profit.
Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-9.2% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 533 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a steep downtrend, down 20% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 47% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 42% and a beta of 0.69, it is more defensive than the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 1.22 vs 5y 0.63), so read it loosely.
About $59.4M trades a day, enough to build a position, and interest is running hot at 1.6x its yearly average volume.
In past sell-offs it fell 39% in the 2020 crash, 13% in the 2022 bear market and 54% in 2008.
val: The stock trades 76% below its DCF fair value of $184, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 45%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $136 to $255 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Technology peers: P/E 9.6 vs 27.4, EV/EBITDA 5.3 vs 17.1 and P/FCF 7.6 vs 26.1 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 36% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are attractive: an FCF yield of 13.2% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 11.4% (vs the 8% bar).
The 3 covering analysts target $57.33 on average, 28% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 16% clears the cost of capital of 8.0% by 8pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have been steady (CV 0.16).
It converts 12% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.47x.
ROE of 14% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.8x equity multiplier).
It spends 2.1% of revenue on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: Leverage is conservative at 0.2x net debt to EBITDA ($514.3M of cash against $646.3M of debt), with interest covered 18.0x.
Goodwill makes up 45% of assets, a soft asset exposed to impairment.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 5.3% over 3 years, 4.1% over 5 years and 3.7% over 10 years.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 0.91 (orders lagging sales), a backlog worth 1.4x annual revenue and deferred revenue down 32%.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (0.8x, 2.1% of sales), a maintenance pace.
Its Rule of 40 score is 14, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
Analysts expect 13.7% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own a modest 1.3%, and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Insider trading is two-way: 1 purchase and 3 sales over the past year, net $309K sold.
It returns 16.6% a year to shareholders (12.0% in buybacks and 5.1% in dividends).
The share count has shrunk 3.5% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
It has paid a dividend for 13 consecutive years, raising it 7.5% a year over the last five.
